title: Count positive readings
prompt: Return how many values are strictly greater than zero. Zero is not positive. Do not change the vector. An empty vector has a count of zero. The vector length fits in int.
driver: int main(){ std::vector<int> values; int x; while(std::cin>>x) values.push_back(x); std::cout<<countPositive(values)<<"\n"; }

tests.label: Only negatives
tests.hint: Negative values do not increase the count.

hints: Keep a count and increase it only for a matching value.
The colon in for (int value : values) means “for each value in values.”
explanation: The loop visits each element once. The const reference borrows the vector for reading. The count is a separate local value.
chapterTitle: Controlling Program Decisions with Conditional Logic
